newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares firm, seen treading water.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares firm, seen treading water.

text.p: Slovenian shares firmed 0.66 percent on Tuesday on what traders said was buying back on growing hopes foreign investors would return to the market.
"Today's slight rise is probably a result of expectations that foreigners will soon return to the market," said one trader.
"But until they do volumes will remain low, while prices will oscillate with the index going up or down by a maximum of 70 points," he added.

The market was sent into a tailspin four weeks ago when the central bank said foreign investors must set up special trading accounts at a fully-licensed Slovenian bank in order to trade in the country's securities.
Since then the blue-chip index has fallen over 16 percent.
Some commercial banks said they have already prepared custody account schemes according to which the cost of the accounts would be about 12 percent of the amount handled.

"We have already prepared our offer and expect to open the first accounts at the end of March," said Alenka Narad, in charge of international investors at the investment banking sector of Slovenia's largest bank Nova Ljubljanska banka (NLB).
She said NLB would be able to handle an inflow of at least 40 million marks ($23 million) this year, but analysts hoped the amount would be larger.

"If major banks decide not to increase the maximum amount of foreign inflow over the accounts, or if foreigners stay away due to the extra cost, liquidity will remain poor and that will push prices down," said Toni Apollonio, an analyst at A banka.
In a worst-case scenario, the index could fall down to around 1,160 points, the analyst added.
The SBI index finished Tuesday's session up 9.03 points at 1,387.24.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded, up 0.45 percent to 56,250 tolars on volume of 172 shares.
Overall 11 shares rose, four fell, three were unchanged and eight were untraded. Turnover fell to 48.3 million tolars from 64.8 million.
Preferred shares of trader Kovinotehna were the top gainers, surging 9.57 percent to 515 on volume of 92 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the leading decliner, closing 4.29 percent lower at 11,820 on volume of six shares.
